items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: We have a parade there on a Sunday, you know. He'd have a white pants.

ctx.x: You could put Joe in a full dress suit and he'd still look undress. You know what he used to do? We have a parade there on a Sunday, you know. He'd have a white pants. He'd come in dirty white pants and take white, white wash and put it on his black shoes. Oh, jeez. It was the frackiest drum player, the frackiest thing in the world. He never had a stiff shirt and he'd look good for him. That's how we call him Rag. Anything you put on, he'd look good for Rag. Nobody's here. It's called Rag. No matter if you can…

Well you know Joe today, right? He still looks that way, man. He'd put a $500 on the floor. He'd put him just like a sock on the roof. Yeah. Is he clearly looking at a sock on the roof? No, he's not union, but he's always a sock on the roof. He put a sock on the roof. I'm going to him. I'm going to him. I love it. Is he a cock-eyed man? Or his brother, is he a cock-eyed man? I don't think, alright? He's not a cock-eyed guy. No, no. He's a two-Steven boy. When I first went to Capco's. You're talking about Louis…
